title: Supersedes gains the ordering half of tier symmetry
subject: supersedes-tier-symmetry
ratio:
`supersedes` gains the ordering half of tier symmetry: a `supersedes` relation whose acting
record's tier number is greater (lower authority) than the target's is a REFUSAL, exit 1.
`supersedes` does not gain SDR-17.9's tier-4-target refusal: overruling a tier-4 note is a
category error because tier 4 binds nobody, but superseding replaces content rather than
overturning force, and replacement of a persuasive note by an equal-or-higher consolidating
successor is exactly the R-12 merge outcome v0 already blesses (`publish --supersedes X --cites
Y`). Conflicts detector 3 widens to scan `supersedes` relations for tier-violating entries (its
documented exclusion DECISION flips with this amendment): a controlling consideration -- the
Overturned-by column's protection of every binding tier from lower-authority status flips -- was
not carried through to the third status-flipping verb, and T-347's live reproduction (a tier-4,
never-verdicted record flipping a tier-1 record's status to superseded, exit 0, zero conflicts
findings) demonstrates the resulting step wrong.
scope_conditions: any supersedes relation published to the registry
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the merge outcome is ever blocked in practice by the ordering check
validity_conditions: publish refuses a supersedes whose acting tier number exceeds the target's
